papers.3: Paper 3 Financial Accounting (A Level structured paper in 2022)

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which item is shown in the equity section of a limited company's statement of financial position?
A 6% loan notes (2033)
B share premium
C corporation tax payable
D dividends paid during the year
parts.answer: B share premium
parts.working: Share premium is a capital reserve and part of equity. Loan notes (A) are a non-current liability; dividends paid (D) appear in the statement of changes in equity as a deduction from retained earnings, not as a separate line in the SOFP.

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP
practice.stem: Shalimar Foods Limited provides the following for the year ended 31 March 2027: revenue $1,840,000; cost of sales $1,104,000; distribution costs $196,000; administrative expenses $248,000; finance costs $36,000; tax $64,000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the gross profit.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the profit from operations.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the profit for the year.
parts.working: 292,000 − finance costs 36,000 = 256,000 profit before tax; − tax 64,000 = 192,000. M1 A1.

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP

parts.label: a
parts.text: State two items that appear in the statement of profit or loss of a limited company but not in that of a sole trader.
parts.answer: Any two: tax (corporation tax / income tax on company profits); directors' remuneration; auditors' fees; loan note (debenture) interest as finance costs.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why dividends paid are not shown as an expense in a company's statement of profit or loss.
parts.answer: Dividends are an appropriation (distribution) of profit to the owners, not a cost of earning profit. They are deducted from retained earnings in the statement of changes in equity.
parts.working: 1 mark: appropriation/distribution to owners, not an expense; 1 mark: shown in SOCE/retained earnings.

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State the heading under which each item appears in a limited company's statement of financial position.
(i) 9% loan notes repayable in 2035
(ii) Tax payable
(iii) General reserve
(iv) Prepaid insurance
parts.answer: (i) non-current liabilities; (ii) current liabilities; (iii) equity; (iv) current assets.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The 9% loan notes become repayable in eight months' time. State how this changes their classification.
parts.answer: They become a current liability (due within 12 months).
parts.working: 1 mark.

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Under which heading are directors' fees shown in a limited company's statement of profit or loss?
A cost of sales
B distribution costs
C administrative expenses
D finance costs
parts.answer: C administrative expenses
parts.working: C: directors' fees relate to running and managing the company, so they are administrative expenses. D is wrong: finance costs are mainly interest on loans and overdrafts, not running costs.

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP
practice.stem: Sarhad Ceramics Limited is preparing its statement of profit or loss.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State the heading in the statement of profit or loss under which each item appears, or state 'not in the statement of profit or loss'.
(i) carriage inwards
(ii) salaries of sales staff
(iii) audit fee
(iv) interest on 7% loan notes
(v) ordinary dividend paid
(vi) depreciation of delivery lorries
parts.answer: (i) cost of sales (ii) distribution costs (iii) administrative expenses (iv) finance costs (v) not in the statement of profit or loss – shown in the statement of changes in equity (vi) distribution costs
parts.working: 1 mark each.

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP
practice.stem:
The following information is available for Rubi Electronics Limited for the year ended 31 December 2026.
Revenue $960,000; inventory 1 January 2026 $74,000; purchases $581,000; inventory 31 December 2026 $86,000; wages and salaries $142,000; depreciation $38,000; other operating expenses $61,500.
The company has $300,000 7% loan notes (2031) in issue for the whole year. Only $10,500 of loan note interest has been paid. Tax for the year is estimated at $29,000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prepare the statement of profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 2026.
parts.answer:
Rubi Electronics Limited                                        
Statement of profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 2026                        
                                                   $           $
Revenue                                                  960,000
Opening inventory                             74,000            
Purchases                                    581,000            
                                             655,000            
Closing inventory                           (86,000)            
Cost of sales                                          (569,000)
Gross profit                                             391,000
Wages and salaries                           142,000            
Depreciation                                  38,000            
Other operating expenses                      61,500            
                                                       (241,500)
Profit from operations                                   149,500
Finance costs (loan note interest)                      (21,000)

parts.label: b

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A company has gross profit $418,000, other operating income (rent received) $9,000, distribution costs $92,000, administrative expenses $133,000 and finance costs $21,000. What is its profit from operations?
A $193,000
B $181,000
C $202,000
D $223,000
parts.working: Profit from operations = 418,000 + 9,000 − 92,000 − 133,000 = 202,000. Finance costs are deducted after profit from operations, so B (181,000) is profit before tax.

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP
practice.stem: Lyallpur Cotton Limited: revenue $742,500; returns inwards $12,600; purchases $455,800; returns outwards $8,900; carriage inwards $6,300; opening inventory $51,200; closing inventory $63,900.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the cost of sales.
parts.working: 51,200 + (455,800 − 8,900) + carriage inwards 6,300 − 63,900 = 440,500. M1 net purchases, M1 carriage inwards added, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the gross profit and the gross margin, correct to two decimal places.
parts.answer: Gross profit $289,400; gross margin 39.65%

parts.label: c
parts.text: State where carriage outwards of $14,700 would be shown.
parts.answer: As an expense (distribution costs) after gross profit, not in cost of sales.
parts.working: 1 mark.

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP
practice.stem:
The following balances relate to Chitral Honey Limited at 31 December 2026 after the statement of profit or loss has been prepared:
                                                                  $
Inventory                                                    41,300
Trade receivables                                            58,600
Allowance for irrecoverable debts: 3% of trade receivables
Insurance prepaid                                             2,400
Cash in hand                                                  3,150
Trade payables                                               47,200
Tax payable                                                  26,800
Loan note interest owing                                      4,500
Bank overdraft                                               12,900
6% loan notes, repayable 30 June 2027                        50,000

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prepare the current assets and current liabilities sections of the statement of financial position at 31 December 2026.
parts.answer: Current assets $103,692; current liabilities $141,400.
parts.working: CA: inventory 41,300; trade receivables 58,600 less allowance 1,758 = 56,842; other receivables (prepayment) 2,400; cash 3,150; total 103,692. CL: trade payables 47,200; tax 26,800; loan note interest accrued 4,500; bank overdraft 12,900; loan notes repayable within 12 months 50,000; total 141,400. 1 mark each correct group, 1 mark totals.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the net current assets (or net current liabilities).
parts.answer: Net current liabilities $37,708

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the loan notes are shown as a current liability this year although they were a non-current liability last year.
parts.answer: They are now repayable within 12 months of the reporting date.

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP
practice.stem:
After preparing the statement of profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 2026, the accountant of Chenab Plastics Limited has the following figures (all adjustments for the year have been posted to profit, but not yet to the asset and liability balances below).
Land at cost $350,000 (not depreciated). Machinery at cost $280,000; accumulated depreciation at 1 January 2026 $96,000; machinery is depreciated at 20% per year on the reducing balance.
Inventory $64,200; trade receivables $52,000, against which an allowance of 5% is to be made; prepaid insurance $2,600; bank $18,300.
Trade payables $47,100; accrued expenses $3,900; tax payable $22,500; 8% loan notes (2032) $150,000.
Ordinary share capital $250,000; share premium $50,000; retained earnings is the only other reserve.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the carrying amount of non-current assets at 31 December 2026.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the net current assets at 31 December 2026.
parts.working: Current assets: inventory 64,200 + receivables 52,000 − allowance 2,600 + prepayment 2,600 + bank 18,300 = 134,500 (M1). Current liabilities 47,100 + 3,900 + 22,500 = 73,500 (M1). Net 61,000 (A1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the retained earnings at 31 December 2026, and state the total equity.
parts.answer: Retained earnings $108,200; total equity $408,200

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP
practice.stem:
Hunza Travel Limited's gross profit for the year ended 30 June 2027 is $512,400. Other balances before adjustments: wages $168,300; rent $54,000; directors' remuneration $96,000; trade receivables $73,500; allowance for irrecoverable debts at 1 July 2026 $2,100; equipment at cost $220,000; 6% loan notes $250,000 (no interest has been paid or recorded).
Additional information:
1 Wages of $4,700 are owing.
2 Rent includes $9,000 paid for July and August 2027.
3 A debt of $3,500 is to be written off. The allowance is to be 4% of the remaining receivables.
4 Equipment is depreciated at 15% per year on cost.
5 Tax for the year is $31,800.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prepare the statement of profit or loss for the year ended 30 June 2027, starting with gross profit.
parts.answer:
Statement of profit or loss (extract), year ended 30 June 2027                        
                                                           $           $
Gross profit                                                     512,400
Wages (168,300 + 4,700)                              173,000            
Rent (54,000 − 9,000)                                 45,000            
Irrecoverable debt                                     3,500            
Increase in allowance for irrecoverable debts            700            
Depreciation of equipment                             33,000            
Directors' remuneration                               96,000            
                                                               (351,200)
Profit from operations                                           161,200
Finance costs                                                   (15,000)
Profit before tax                                                146,200
Tax                                                             (31,800)
Profit for the year                                              114,400
parts.working: Wages 173,000 (1); rent 45,000 (1); irrecoverable debt 3,500 (1); allowance 4% × 70,000 = 2,800, increase 700 (2); depreciation 33,000 (1); directors' remuneration (1); finance costs 6% × 250,000 = 15,000 (1); profit for the year 114,400 (1).

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A company's profit before tax is $140,000. Last year's tax liability was estimated at $24,000 but $25,600 was paid in settlement this year. Tax on this year's profit is estimated at $31,000. What is the profit for the year?
A $109,000
B $107,400
C $110,600
D $114,400
parts.working: B: tax charge = current estimate 31,000 + under-provision 1,600 = 32,600; 140,000 − 32,600 = 107,400. A ignores the under-provision from last year.

practice.subtopic: Statement of profit or loss and SOFP
practice.stem:
Extract from the trial balance of Saffron Spices Limited at 31 December 2026:
                                                                     $
Revenue                                                      1,260,000
Purchases                                                      742,000
Inventory at 1 January 2026                                     86,000
Carriage inwards                                                 8,400
Wages and salaries                                             196,000
Rent                                                            48,000
Directors' fees                                                 72,000
Advertising                                                     31,500
Delivery vans at cost                                          120,000
Delivery vans – accumulated depreciation at 1 January 2026      45,000
Office equipment at cost                                        64,000
8% loan notes (issued several years ago)                       150,000
Loan note interest paid                                          6,000
Additional information:
1 Inventory at 31 December 2026 was $94,500.
2 Wages and salaries are 40% distribution and 60% administration.
3 Rent includes $4,000 paid in advance for 2027. Rent is an administrative expense.
4 Delivery vans are depreciated at 25% per year reducing balance; office equipment at 10% per year on cost.
5 Tax on the profit for the year is estimated at $38,000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prepare the statement of profit or loss of Saffron Spices Limited for the year ended 31 December 2026.
parts.answer: Cost of sales $741,900; gross profit $518,100; distribution costs $128,650; administrative expenses $240,000; profit from operations $149,450; finance costs $12,000; profit before tax $137,450; tax $38,000; profit for the year $99,450.
parts.working: Cost of sales 86,000 + 742,000 + 8,400 − 94,500 = 741,900 (2). Distribution: wages 78,400 + advertising 31,500 + van depreciation (120,000 − 45,000) × 25% = 18,750; total 128,650 (2). Administrative: wages 117,600 + rent 44,000 + directors' fees 72,000 + equipment depreciation 6,400; total 240,000 (2). Profit from operations 149,450 (1). Finance costs 150,000 × 8% = 12,000 (1). Tax 38,000, profit for the year 99,450 (1). Correct headings/format (1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the amount of loan note interest that will appear in the statement of financial position at 31 December 2026, and its heading.
parts.answer: $6,000 under current liabilities (other payables / accruals).
parts.working: 12,000 − 6,000 paid = 6,000 (B1); current liability (B1).

practice.stem:
At 1 January 2026, Kohsar Pharma Limited had: ordinary shares of $1 each $300,000; share premium $45,000; retained earnings $162,000.
During 2026 the company issued 100,000 ordinary shares at $1.60 each, fully paid in cash. Profit for the year was $88,500. Dividends paid during the year were $36,000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prepare the statement of changes in equity for the year ended 31 December 2026.
parts.answer:
Statement of changes in equity, year ended 31 Dec 2026                                                
                                Share cap. Share prem.  Ret. earn.       Total
                                         $           $           $           $
At 1 January 2026                  300,000      45,000     162,000     507,000
Share issue                        100,000      60,000                 160,000
Profit for the year                                         88,500      88,500
Dividends paid                                            (36,000)    (36,000)
At 31 December 2026                400,000     105,000     214,500     719,500
parts.working: Opening balances (1); share capital +100,000 (1); premium +60,000 (1); profit (1); dividends (1); closing balances (1).

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which transaction increases the total equity shown in a company's statement of changes in equity?
A a bonus issue of shares
B a transfer from retained earnings to general reserve
C a rights issue of shares
D payment of an interim dividend
parts.answer: C a rights issue of shares
parts.working: C: a rights issue brings in cash from shareholders, increasing share capital (and share premium). A is wrong: a bonus issue only moves amounts between reserves and share capital, so total equity is unchanged.

practice.stem: Pak Fresh Juices Limited has ordinary shares of $0.50 each. During the year ended 31 March 2027 it issued shares for cash. Its share capital rose from $500,000 to $650,000 and its share premium from $60,000 to $105,000. Profit for the year was $71,200 and dividends paid were $32,500. Retained earnings at 31 March 2027 were $187,400.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of shares issued during the year and the issue price per share.
parts.answer: 300,000 shares at $0.65 each.
parts.working: Share capital increase 150,000 ÷ $0.50 = 300,000 shares (M1 A1); cash received 150,000 + premium 45,000 = 195,000; ÷ 300,000 = $0.65 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the retained earnings at 1 April 2026.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the purpose of a statement of changes in equity.
parts.answer: To show the movement in each component of equity (share capital and each reserve) between the start and end of the period.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
For each of the following, state the column(s) of the statement of changes in equity affected and whether each increases or decreases:
(i) profit for the year
(ii) issue of shares at a premium for cash
(iii) a bonus issue made from the general reserve
(iv) upward revaluation of land
(v) dividends paid
parts.answer: (i) retained earnings increase (ii) share capital increase and share premium increase (iii) share capital increase, general reserve decrease (iv) revaluation reserve increase (v) retained earnings decrease
parts.working: 1 mark each.

practice.stem:
At 1 April 2026, Ravi Textiles Limited had: ordinary shares of $0.50 each $800,000; share premium $120,000; retained earnings $410,000.
During the year ended 31 March 2027:
1 On 1 June 2026 a bonus issue of 1 share for every 4 held was made, using the share premium as far as possible and then retained earnings.
2 On 1 October 2026 a rights issue of 1 share for every 5 held was made at $0.80 per share. All rights were taken up.
3 Profit for the year was $236,000 and dividends paid were $95,000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of shares issued (i) in the bonus issue and (ii) in the rights issue.
parts.answer: (i) 400,000 shares; (ii) 400,000 shares
parts.working: Shares at start 800,000 ÷ 0.50 = 1,600,000; bonus 1 for 4 = 400,000; after bonus 2,000,000; rights 1 for 5 = 400,000.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Prepare the statement of changes in equity for the year ended 31 March 2027.
parts.working: Bonus issue 200,000 (1) funded from share premium 120,000 (1) and retained earnings 80,000 (1); rights issue share capital 200,000 (1) and premium 120,000 (1); profit and dividends (1); closing balances (2).

practice.stem:
Hamza Logistics Limited, at 1 July 2026: ordinary share capital $600,000; general reserve $75,000; retained earnings $288,000.
During the year to 30 June 2027 land was revalued upwards by $140,000. Profit for the year was $112,000. Dividends of $48,000 were paid. The directors transferred $25,000 to the general reserve.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prepare the statement of changes in equity for the year ended 30 June 2027.
parts.answer:
Share cap.  Gen. res.Reval. res. Ret. earn.      Total
                                      $          $          $          $          $
At 1 July 2026                  600,000     75,000               288,000    963,000
Revaluation of land                                   140,000               140,000
Profit for the year                                              112,000    112,000
Dividends paid                                                  (48,000)   (48,000)
Transfer to general reserve                 25,000              (25,000)          0
At 30 June 2027                 600,000    100,000    140,000    327,000  1,167,000
parts.working: Columns and opening balances (1); revaluation reserve (1); profit (1); dividends (1); transfer shown in both columns with no effect on total (1); closing balances (1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the transfer to general reserve does not change total equity.
parts.answer: It moves profit from retained earnings to another revenue reserve within equity; no assets or liabilities change, so total equity is the same.
parts.working: 1 mark: movement between reserves; 1 mark: no change to net assets.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which item is shown in a company's statement of changes in equity but NOT in its statement of profit or loss?
A loan note interest
B tax on profit
C dividends paid
D directors' fees
parts.answer: C dividends paid
parts.working: Dividends paid are a distribution to shareholders recorded in the SOCE (reducing retained earnings). Loan note interest (A) is a finance cost in the statement of profit or loss.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Retained earnings at the start of the year were $214,000. During the year: profit for the year $96,500; interim dividend paid $18,000; last year's final dividend paid $27,000; transfer to general reserve $20,000; land revalued upwards by $35,000. A final dividend of $30,000 was proposed after the year end. What are the retained earnings at the end of the year?
A $245,500
B $280,500
C $215,500
D $265,500
parts.working: A: 214,000 + 96,500 − 18,000 − 27,000 − 20,000 = 245,500. The revaluation goes to the revaluation reserve (B is wrong) and the proposed dividend is not a liability at the year end (C).

practice.stem:
Sialkot Packaging Limited had the following equity at 1 July 2026: ordinary shares of $0.50 each $800,000; share premium $64,000; revaluation reserve $40,000; retained earnings $210,000. During the year ended 30 June 2027:
• October 2026: issued 200,000 new ordinary shares at $0.90 each for cash, fully paid.
• January 2027: the factory was revalued upwards by $55,000.
• March 2027: $20,000 was transferred from retained earnings to a general reserve (there was no general reserve before).
• Profit for the year was $146,000.
• April 2027: an interim dividend of 4 cents per share was paid on all shares in issue at that date.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the dividend paid during the year and the share premium arising from the October 2026 share issue.
parts.answer: Dividend $72,000; share premium $80,000.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Prepare the statement of changes in equity for the year ended 30 June 2027.
parts.answer: Share capital $900,000; share premium $144,000; revaluation reserve $95,000; general reserve $20,000; retained earnings $264,000; total equity $1,423,000.
parts.working: Opening balances (1); share issue: share capital +100,000 and share premium +80,000 (1); revaluation +55,000 to revaluation reserve (1); transfer 20,000 from retained earnings to general reserve (1); profit 146,000 less dividend 72,000 in retained earnings (1); column totals and total equity (1).

practice.stem:
Kirthar Glass Limited had the following equity at 1 January 2026: ordinary shares of $1 each $800,000; share premium $50,000; general reserve $90,000; retained earnings $274,000.
During 2026:
• In March a bonus issue of 1 share for every 8 held was made, using the whole share premium first and the balance from the general reserve.
• In June land was revalued from $210,000 to $275,000.
• Profit for the year was $132,000.
• $30,000 was transferred to the general reserve.
• In October a dividend of 5 cents per share was paid on all shares then in issue.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Prepare the statement of changes in equity for the year ended 31 December 2026.
parts.answer: Closing: share capital 900,000; share premium 0; general reserve 70,000; revaluation reserve 65,000; retained earnings 331,000; total 1,366,000.
parts.working: Bonus issue 100,000: share premium −50,000, general reserve −50,000, share capital +100,000 (2). Revaluation +65,000 (1). Profit 132,000 (1). Transfer 30,000 RE→GR (1). Dividend 5c × 900,000 = 45,000 (1). Totals (1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the change in total equity during the year, and explain why the bonus issue did not contribute to it.
parts.answer: Increase of $152,000. A bonus issue only converts reserves into share capital; no cash is received, so total equity is unchanged.

practice.stem:
Equity of Lasbela Fisheries Limited (ordinary shares of $1):
                         31 March 2027 $   31 March 2026 $
Ordinary share capital           600,000           500,000
General reserve                   20,000           120,000
Retained earnings                263,000           192,500
Dividends of $48,000 were paid during the year. There were no other movements.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the profit for the year ended 31 March 2027.
parts.working: Retained earnings 263,000 − 192,500 + dividends 48,000 = 118,500 (M1 A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The increase in share capital was a bonus issue. Calculate the ratio of the bonus issue and state which reserve was used.
parts.answer: 1 for 5; the general reserve (which fell by the same $100,000).
parts.working: 100,000 ÷ 500,000 = 1 new for every 5 held (B1); general reserve 120,000 → 20,000 (B1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the dividend per share paid in the year, assuming it was paid after the bonus issue.
parts.answer: 8 cents per share.

practice.stem:
Extract from the records of Thar Minerals Limited for the year ended 31 December 2026.
Retained earnings 1 January 2026 $184,500; retained earnings 31 December 2026 $226,900.
During 2026: the final dividend for 2025 of $42,000 and an interim dividend of $18,000 were paid; $30,000 was transferred to general reserve; a bonus issue used $25,000 of retained earnings. No other items affected retained earnings apart from the profit for the year.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the profit for the year ended 31 December 2026.
parts.working: Closing RE 226,900 = opening 184,500 + profit − final dividend 42,000 − interim 18,000 − transfer 30,000 − bonus 25,000. Profit = 226,900 − 184,500 + 60,000 + 30,000 + 25,000 = 157,400. M1 dividends, M1 transfer, M1 bonus, A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the final dividend for 2026, proposed in February 2027, is not deducted in the 2026 statement of changes in equity.
parts.answer: A dividend proposed after the reporting date is not a liability at 31 December 2026 (no obligation exists until approved), so it is only disclosed in a note and recorded when paid/approved in 2027 (IAS 10).
parts.working: 1 mark: not a liability/obligation at year end; 1 mark: disclosed as a note.

practice.stem:
Kalash Cement Limited has an issued share capital of 2,000,000 ordinary shares of $1 each. At 1 January 2027: share premium $150,000; retained earnings $520,000.
• 15 March 2027: paid the final dividend for 2026 of 5 cents per share.
• 1 May 2027: rights issue of 1 share for every 4 held at $1.20, fully taken up.
• 1 September 2027: paid an interim dividend of 3 cents per share.
Profit for the year ended 31 December 2027 was $274,000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the total dividends paid during 2027.

Share cap. Share prem.  Ret. earn.       Total
                                       $           $           $           $
